data.description:
# Record the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract for client logic

## Problem statement

The withdrawn drain-before-cheap feature failed because client logic hardcoded
a cheap-pool budget (`freeSlots >= 2`) that silently contradicted the live proxy
config, where the cheap pool had already been raised from 2 to 3 slots and fast
held 1 — the inverse of the brief's assumption. No single document states the
current per-mode slot counts, where they are defined, or the rule that client
code must never hardcode them, so the same drift can silently recur.

## Users

- **Agent/plugin developers** writing or reviewing client logic that consumes
  the llama-proxy (herdr mode-switch worker, downtime dispatcher, audit fan-out)
  — need one authoritative statement of the slot-count contract so they derive
  capacity from live status instead of baking in constants.
- **Future maintainers** changing a mode profile — need to know that a slot-count
  change is a contract change with downstream client impact, and where the
  authoritative values live.

User story:

- *As a developer of proxy-consuming client logic, I want a single documented
  contract for fast/cheap slot counts and their source files, so that I derive
  capacity from the live proxy status rather than hardcoding a pool size that
  silently drifts out of date.*

## Existing state

- `llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml` — authoritative base config;
  `session_slot_pool_size: 1`.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config-fast.yaml` — fast-mode **overlay**; does **not**
  override `session_slot_pool_size`, so fast inherits **1** from the base.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — cheap-mode **overlay**;
  `session_slot_pool_size: 3` overrides the base, so cheap has **3** slots.
- Overlays are deep-merged onto the base by `load_config()` /
  `proxy.config_merge.deep_merge`; deleting an overlay degrades the profile to
  the base profile.
- **Known stale prose (evidence of the drift risk):**
  - `llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml` inline comment still claims
    "default/fast: 3, cheap: 2" immediately below the actual `1` value.
  - `ContextHub/docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` §1 Goal still states
    "fast (cloud-backed, 3-slot pool) and cheap (2-slot local-first pool)",
    while the same document's "Withdrawn client drain" section correctly states
    fast = 1 slot, cheap = 3 slots.
- Change history: fast/default and cheap were set to **1 / 3** in
  `llm-manager` commit `8567bcbb` (LP-0MU03AL730000B5W); previously cheap was
  **2**. The drain feature (WL-0MUL0KO7Q003O7YJ) was built against the stale
  2-slot assumption and was withdrawn (WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR,
  WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM).

## Desired change

- Publish the slot-count contract in the proxy documentation (the
  `llm-manager/proxy/README.md` "Slot configuration" section is the natural
  authoritative home; alternatively a `docs/design` note) covering:
  - Current counts: **fast/default = 1 slot; cheap = 3 slots**.
  - Exact source locations: `proxy/config.yaml` (base; `1`),
    `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (overlay; `3`), and that `config-fast.yaml`
    intentionally does not override.
  - The base+overlay merge semantics that make the effective value what it is.
  - **The contract:** client/proxy-consumer logic MUST NOT hardcode pool
    sizes; it derives capacity from the live proxy status (or does not depend
    on a slot count at all).
  - Change history (cheap 2 -> 3, fast/default -> 1) and the silent-drift risk.
- Add a **pointer** from `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` to the contract,
  and correct that document's stale "3-slot fast / 2-slot cheap" goal sentence.
- Documentation only — no production code change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The slot-count contract is documented with current values (fast/default
      = 1, cheap = 3) and both source locations (`proxy/config.yaml` base,
      `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` overlay), plus the fact that
      `config-fast.yaml` does not override.
- [ ] The documented contract states explicitly that client/proxy-consumer
      logic MUST NOT hardcode pool sizes and must derive capacity from live
      status (or not depend on a slot count).
- [ ] A pointer to the contract exists from
      `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, and that document's stale
      "fast 3-slot / cheap 2-slot" goal statement is corrected to
      fast = 1 / cheap = 3.
- [ ] Change history (cheap 2 -> 3, fast/default -> 1) and the silent-drift
      risk are recorded.
- [ ] No production code change (documentation-only diff).
- [ ] A review/validation step confirms the documented values match the live
      config files (e.g. by grep or a cited source location).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Documentation-only: no production code change.
- The authoritative values live in the sibling `llm-manager` repo
  (`proxy/config*.yaml`). The contract text in ContextHub must cite those
  paths and values; if the proxy docs are edited, that is a separate repo and
  should be coordinated/committed there.
- Do not restate a slot count in client code comments in a way that can drift;
  the contract prefers derivation from live status.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Drift risk (the motivating risk):** a slot-count change in
  `llm-manager/proxy/*.yaml` can silently invalidate client assumptions; the
  contract is the mitigation, not a hard guarantee. Mitigation: point at source
  files and mandate live-status derivation.
- **Two-repo split:** the proxy config lives in `llm-manager`, the design doc
  in `ContextHub`. Assumption: the primary contract lives alongside the proxy
  config (or ContextHub cites it); either way the pointer from
  `mode-switch-worker.md` stays in ContextHub.
- **Scope creep:** other stale slot prose (config.yaml inline comment,
  downtime dispatcher docs) may surface. Record extra fixes as linked work
  items rather than expanding this doc-only item's scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `llm-manager/proxy/README.md` — authoritative slot-configuration section;
  add the contract, values, sources, and change history.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml` — base value (`session_slot_pool_size: 1`);
  correct the stale "default/fast: 3, cheap: 2" inline comment.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config-cheap.yaml` — overlay value (`3`); cite as source.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config-fast.yaml` — cite as "no override".
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` — add contract pointer; fix the stale
  "3-slot fast / 2-slot cheap" goal sentence.

## Related work

- WL-0MUL0KO7Q003O7YJ — Drain before switching to cheap (withdrawn; built on
  the stale 2-slot cheap assumption).
- WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM — Drain-before-cheap threshold unsatisfiable in fast
  mode (1-slot pool).
- WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR — Revert drain-before-cheap.
- LP-0MU03AL730000B5W (llm-manager) — Slot counts: default and fast -> 1,
  cheap -> 3 (the originating change, commit `8567bcbb`).
- LP-0MSLLDC5L003W8Q3 (llm-manager) — proxy-usage-analysis: remove hardcoded
  slot counts.
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` — mode-switch design (needs the pointer
  and stale-prose fix).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

_No interview questions were required._ The seed brief (title, why, scope with
exact values and source paths, and testable ACs) was sufficient to draft a
clear intake; repo inspection confirmed every stated value:

- `llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml` line 864: `session_slot_pool_size: 1`.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config-cheap.yaml` line 34: `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.
- `llm-manager/proxy/config-fast.yaml`: no `session_slot_pool_size` key
  (inherits 1).
- `llm-manager` commit `8567bcbb` changed cheap 2 -> 3 and default/fast to 1.

Open questions: none.
